composition.summary: An irregular Heartlands oak-meadow basin centered on a shallow loam hollow and dry streambed, with a western meadow, eastern coppice clearing, northern fieldstone overlook, and branching figure-eight paths.
visualHierarchy: The warm ochre loam hollow and dry streambed form the low central seam and shared crossing space.
The broad western meadow balances the denser eastern coppice clearing as distinct formation grounds.
A low northern fieldstone overlook crowns the upper loop without becoming an isolated peak.
Oak, flowering hawthorn, field maple, and rounded fieldstone shape an organic pastoral boundary.
focalAreas: central shallow loam hollow and dry streambed
negativeSpace: Keep open breathing room within the western meadow and eastern coppice clearing for readable formations.
Preserve sightlines through the shallow hollow and around both figure-eight crossings.
Leave narrow natural gaps between hawthorn, oak, and fieldstone boundary clusters for alternate approaches.
density: Open warm meadow grass and bluebells across the western basin shelf.
Moderate coppiced oak, field maple, leaf litter, and low fieldstone density around the eastern clearing.
Denser oak and flowering hawthorn clusters along the irregular outer basin rim.
Sparse fieldstone accents on the northern overlook and beside streambed crossings.

areas.description: A broad, shallow loam depression and dry streambed that carries the middle crossing without functioning as a choke.
An irregular open meadow formation area with multiple exits into both halves of the figure-eight network.
A sheltered formation clearing edged by coppiced oak and field maple with distinct upper and lower approaches.
A broad low overlook backed by rounded fieldstone and reached by natural slopes or occasional fieldstone stairs.
A low path fork framed by flowering hawthorn that closes the lower loop and provides a second cross-basin route.

descending upper-loop branches around oak and fieldstone clusters

secondary upper branch that creates the northern crossing

connections: Use natural grassy or loamy slopes for most level changes.
Use occasional rounded fieldstone stairs where the upper loop meets the northern overlook.
Keep every rise broad and connected; do not create isolated peaks.
Let the dry streambed remain shallow enough to cross at several readable points.

primaryApproaches: Build two interlocking loops between the western meadow and eastern coppice clearing, crossing through the central hollow and reconnecting at northern and southern branches.
Give each formation area at least two tactically distinct approaches, with no route serving as the sole crossing.
Curve paths around oak, hawthorn, and fieldstone clusters instead of forming straight corridors.
secondaryApproaches: Link the northern overlook to both sides of the basin by a slope route and an occasional fieldstone-stair route.
Use the southern hawthorn fork and shallow streambed branches to preserve flanking choices around the lower loop.
Keep both figure-eight crossing spaces broad enough for alternate movement lines.

Do not make either formation depend on a single choke or crossing.

natural slopes and occasional fieldstone stairs

composition.summary: An irregular Heartlands forest hollow organized around an enormous storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass spanning a shallow diagonal dry ravine, with a broad southwest clover glade, smaller northeast fern-and-hazel glade, northwest fieldstone terrace, and southeast hawthorn loop.
visualHierarchy: The enormous storm-fallen ancient oak, shattered trunk, and exposed root mass dominate the central diagonal dry ravine without dividing the map into disconnected halves.
A broad sunlit clover glade in the southwest provides the principal open formation ground.
A smaller fern-and-hazel glade in the northeast provides a sheltered opposing formation ground.
A low northwest fieldstone terrace and a southeast hawthorn loop frame two outer reconnecting approaches.
Ancient oak, hazel, hawthorn, fern banks, roots, and rounded fieldstone shape an organic forest-owned boundary.
focalAreas: storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass
broad southwest sunlit clover formation glade
northwest low fieldstone terrace and lookout
negativeSpace: Keep broad irregular breathing room inside the southwest clover glade and smaller northeast fern-and-hazel glade for readable formations.
Preserve navigable gaps around and beneath the fallen trunk and exposed root seam so the landmark never becomes a single choke.
Keep the northwest terrace and southeast hawthorn loop visually open enough to read as distinct reconnecting approaches.
Do not turn the dry ravine into water or a straight cleared strip.
density: Open sunlit clover and warm meadow grass across the broad southwest glade.
Moderate ferns, hazel stools, leaf litter, and dappled shade around the smaller northeast glade.
Dense ancient oak, hazel, hawthorn, root, and fern masses along the irregular outer forest edge.
Sparse rounded fieldstone on the low northwest terrace and at a few gentle level transitions.

areas.description: An enormous storm-fallen ancient oak and exposed root mass spanning the shallow diagonal dry ravine, with broad navigable passages around and beneath it.
A broad irregular sunlit clover formation glade with distinct entries into the central, northwest, and southeast approaches.
A smaller sheltered formation glade edged by ferns and hazel, with distinct entries from the oak seam, northwest terrace, and southeast loop.
A broad low fieldstone terrace and lookout reached by gentle slopes and a few fieldstone stairs, never an isolated peak.
A curving low route enclosed by irregular hawthorn clusters that reconnects both glades around the southeast side.

composition.summary: An irregular limestone cavern organized around a shallow central sink, a broad southern formation chamber, a smaller northern grotto, and western and eastern shelves joined by three reconnecting natural passages.
visualHierarchy: A broad southern limestone chamber anchors the scene and provides the principal open formation ground without touching a flat map edge.
A smaller northern crystal-lit grotto provides a distinct opposing formation ground.
A shallow central sink with broken limestone columns divides sightlines without becoming an impassable moat.
Western flowstone terraces and an eastern stalagmite shelf frame two outer approaches that reconnect beyond the sink.
Layered cavern walls, stalagmites, rubble, and shadowed fissures own the irregular outer boundary.
focalAreas: shallow central sink and broken limestone columns
negativeSpace: Keep irregular open floor inside both formation caverns for readable tactical groupings.
Preserve broad navigable gaps around both sides of the central sink and broken columns.
Keep passage mouths and elevation transitions visually separate from solid cavern walls.
Avoid large featureless black voids that obscure the playable silhouette.
density: Open pale limestone floor in the southern chamber.
Moderate crystal, calcite, and rubble detail around the northern grotto and route junctions.
Dense stalagmites, broken columns, flowstone, and dark rock along the irregular boundary.
Sparse floor accents inside movement lanes and formation clearings.

areas.description: A broad irregular limestone chamber with maneuvering room and three distinct exits.
A smaller elevated grotto with local cover and three distinct entries.
A shallow crossable depression with broken columns and multiple passages around its edges.
A broad connected limestone shelf reached by natural ramps and a short carved stair.
A lower curving shelf whose stalagmite clusters shape cover without closing the route.

Keep every shelf connected; do not create isolated rock pillars or detached platforms.

primaryApproaches: Provide three tactically distinct route families between the formation caverns: through the central sink, across the western terrace, and around the eastern shelf.
Keep three independent passage mouths at both formation caverns; interconnect the route families only at multiple mid-map junctions without merging them into a shared throat near either formation.
Bend routes around limestone columns, stalagmites, shelves, and rubble rather than drawing straight mine corridors.
secondaryApproaches: Branch both outer shelves back toward the central sink to prevent corridor play.
Use a mixture of broad ramps and short stairs so elevation changes remain readable.
Preserve multiple passage mouths around every major landmark.

boundaryIntent.description: Natural limestone walls, flowstone, stalagmites, rubble, and shadowed fissures own an uneven cave edge; never resolve the playable or rendered perimeter into a rectangular room or continuous constructed wall.

spawnIntent.formationCharacter: Opposing formations occupy the broad southern cavern and smaller northern grotto, each with local cover, irregular maneuvering room, and access to all three reconnecting passage families.
